successors.name: Lesotho
successors.text: 'the boundaries of present-day Lesotho (previously Basutoland) were then drawn up' in February 1869

ledger.x: 1822: Moshoeshoe becomes the first king of the Basotho.
19 March 1858: the Orange Free State declares war on the Basotho over the Caledon lands.
1 June 1858: an armistice ends the first war.
1865: the Free State launches the Seqiti War.
11 April 1866: Moshoeshoe accepts the peace of Thaba Bosiu.
12 March 1868: Britain takes Moshoeshoe's people under its protection.
February 1869: the Convention of Aliwal North ends the Free State wars.
February 1869: the Conquered Territory goes to the Orange Free State.
1871: Basutoland is annexed to the Cape Colony.
1880: the Basuto Gun War breaks out against Cape rule.
1881: the Gun War ends; the Cape's rule is replaced by imperial administration in 1884.
2 February 1884: Basutoland returns from the Cape to direct imperial administration.
4 October 1966: Basutoland becomes independent as Lesotho.

wars.name: Free State-Basotho Wars
wars.outcome: Senekal's War (1858), the Seqiti War (1865-66) and the Third Basotho War (1867-68): armistice 1 June 1858; peace of Thaba Bosiu 11 April 1866; British protection 12 March 1868; the Convention of Aliwal North (February 1869) fixed the boundary and gave the…

wars.name: Basuto Gun War
wars.outcome: Revolt against Cape rule over Basutoland after the Cape annexation of 1871; the colony returned to imperial administration in 1884.

certainty.note: Kingdom's frontier was disputed; the Warden Line (1849), the 1858 armistice and the 1866 'frontier line' were not accepted by Moshoeshoe.
Boundaries fixed by the Convention of Aliwal North, February 1869.
